title: A complex is pseudo-coherent exactly when it is m-pseudo-coherent for all m, and then its finite free resolution can be chosen to vanish above the top cohomology
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes pseudo-coherence of a complex K over an arbitrary ring in three equivalent ways and appends a vanishing refinement: if the cohomology of K vanishes above b, then the quasi-isomorphism from a bounded above complex of finite free modules to K can be chosen with the same vanishing bound (statement lines 16049-16059). The direction (3) => (1) is not a citation but a construction: a bounded above complex of finite projective modules is rebuilt as one of finite free modules by the telescoping direct sum decompositions in the top degree and one degree lower, arranged so that the comparison map is even a homotopy equivalence (proof lines 16064-16076). The substantial part is (2) => (3) together with the vanishing bound, a descending induction on n in which finite free modules, their differentials and compatible maps to K are built so that the comparison map on cohomology is an isomorphism above n and surjective in degree n; the induction step passes through the cone on the partially built map, the long exact cohomology sequence, and the two cited lemmas lemma-cone-pseudo-coherent and lemma-finite-cohomology, and then needs a final correction of the module in degree n - 1 by a free summand in order to kill the cokernel there (proof lines 16086-16141). The bookkeeping of two cohomological properties plus a vanishing range at once, with the correction step at the end, is what keeps this out of the routine range; no step of the argument is replaced by a citation.
